questions.help: Drives Social Security claiming optimization, survivor-benefit planning, and the widow's tax-trap exposure assessment. The higher-earner spouse delaying SS to 70 while the lower-earner files at FRA is the standard high-leverage decumulation play.

questions.label: If your portfolio dropped 35% in a single year (2008-style), what would you most likely do?
questions.help: No "right" answer here — we calibrate the framework's recommendations to how you actually invest, not how the textbook says you should. Reframed per behavioral-economics evidence on social-desirability bias in normatively-ranked options.

options.l: Add to equity (deploy cash or rebalance into the drop)

questions.label: Looking back at March 2020 (COVID drawdown), the 2022 bear market, or 2008 if you were investing then — what did you actually do in the worst of it?
questions.help: Affective forecasting evidence (Wilson-Gilbert 2003; Frydman-Rangel 2014) shows people systematically over-predict their composure under future financial stress; past behavior is a stronger signal than predicted behavior. When both are available, the framework weights this answer more heavily.

options.l: Added to equity (deployed cash or rebalanced into the drop)
Reduced equity allocation during the drawdown
I wasn't investing during any of those events

questions.help: Lusardi-Mitchell "Big Three" financial-literacy probe (interest compounding). Calibrates downstream presentation to your baseline. No "right" answer punishment — wrong answers just unlock more foundational explanations in your Plan output.

options.l: I don't know / prefer not to guess

questions.help: Lusardi-Mitchell Big Three #2 (inflation effect on purchasing power).

questions.label: Suppose you owe $1,000 on a credit card and the interest rate is 20% per year, compounded annually. If you make no payments and no new charges, how many years would it take for the debt to double?
questions.help: Lusardi-Tufano debt-literacy item (Rule of 72 inverse): at 20%, 72/20 ≈ 3.6 years.

questions.help: Qualifying nonprofit or government employment for Public Service Loan Forgiveness

questions.label: Have you ever audited your IDR / PSLF payment history at studentaid.gov?
questions.help: Federal loan servicers (Navient, MOHELA, Nelnet) have been the subject of CFPB enforcement actions documenting systematic mis-tracking of qualifying payments. Pulling your full payment history and reconciling it is often the highest-NPV financial action available to federal student loan borrowers — sometimes worth $40K–$80K in retroactive PSLF or IDR forgiveness credit.

options.l: Yes — within the past year, no discrepancies
Yes — found discrepancies, working with servicer/CFPB

questions.label: If on income-driven repayment, which plan are you currently enrolled in?
questions.help: SAVE-enrolled borrowers were placed in administrative forbearance during the 2024–2025 litigation; forbearance months do NOT count toward PSLF or IDR forgiveness. Every month of inaction has direct dollar cost — this question routes whether the framework surfaces a SAVE-specific switch action. OBBBA sunsets SAVE, PAYE, and ICR by July 1, 2028 (migration to IBR or the new RAP), so PAYE/ICR answers route migration-planning actions too.

options.l: RAP (Repayment Assistance Plan — new under OBBBA, opens July 2026)

questions.label: Do you have meaningful Traditional / pre-tax retirement balances (401(k), 403(b), Traditional IRA) and an early-retirement window before Social Security and RMDs begin?
questions.help: Roth conversions during the "tax valley" between retirement and RMD age (73 now, rising to 75 in 2033 per SECURE 2.0) are one of the highest-NPV decumulation moves available — a typical conversion ladder of $300K-$500K filling the 12% bracket from a household otherwise pulled into 22-24% by SS + RMDs saves $30K-$60K in lifetime federal tax (Kitces NEV).

options.l: Yes — meaningful Trad balances and a window of lower-income years before SS / RMDs
Meaningful Trad balances but already claiming SS / at RMD age
Low or no Traditional pre-tax balances (mostly Roth or taxable)
Not sure — need to look at account balances

questions.label: Does your employer offer a 401(k) / 403(b) match?
Are you contributing enough to capture the full match?
Does your 401(k) plan offer automatic annual contribution escalation, and is it enabled?
questions.help: Auto-escalation (Thaler-Benartzi "Save More Tomorrow" 2004) pre-commits future-you to a 1–2pp/yr increase, capped at a target rate. SECURE 2.0 made this default-on for new plans starting 2025.

options.l: Yes, available but I haven't enabled it

questions.label: What is the lowest expense ratio available in your 401(k) plan?
questions.help: Small-employer plans often have all-in expenses 3–5× higher than large-employer plans (DOL Form 5500 / Brightscope-ICI data). Affects whether the Bogleheads framework is actionable inside your 401(k) or whether you should weight toward the IRA for low-cost index funds.

options.l: Under 0.10% (typical large-employer plan with broad index funds)
0.30–0.60% (workable, weight toward IRA for asset location)
Above 0.60% (poor menu — capture match, weight other contributions toward IRA)
I don't know — need to look it up

questions.label: Do you own rental real estate or are you exploring a short-term rental (STR)?
questions.help: Routes Phase 7 §4 (cost-seg + REPS + STR loophole) coverage. Most W-2 households who first encountered the STR loophole on personal-finance social media should NOT pursue it — the cost-seg-firm and STR-coaching-program ecosystem is heavily commission-driven and the IRS audit posture has tightened. This question routes you into the defensive-reading version of AdvStrat §4, not into a recommendation to engage the strategy.

options.l: No rental real estate, not exploring
Exploring STR after seeing it discussed online

questions.label: Are you likely to provide financial support to aging parents in the next 10–15 years?
questions.help: Median sandwich-generation cost runs $50K–$200K per parent in adult-child financial contribution per Genworth/MetLife caregiver studies — material enough to surface as a planning line item.

options.l: Yes, substantial — likely to provide significant ongoing support
Yes, modest — some support likely but not the primary funding source
Unlikely — parents independently funded but not certain
Parents deceased or independently funded with high certainty

questions.label: Approximate annual after-tax household expenses
questions.help: Drives every downstream calculator that needs a spending figure — SWR target, FI math, DIME sizing, retirement-replacement-rate.

questions.label: Roughly what fraction of your annual expenses are essential (housing, healthcare, basic food, insurance, transportation to essential places) vs discretionary (travel, entertainment, gifting, lifestyle)?
questions.help: Determines whether dynamic-withdrawal or guardrails strategies are feasible (they require cuttable discretionary) and the right LTC / DI sizing target (which is the essential portion, not the total).

options.l: 90%+ essential — almost all spending is non-cuttable
Under 50% essential — substantial discretionary, high flexibility

questions.label: Are you and your spouse aligned on your target savings rate?
questions.help: Within-household disagreement about saving rate is one of the strongest predictors of plan-execution failure per Yilmazer-Lyons 2010 and Bertocchi-Brunetti-Torricelli 2014. The framework's optimization recommendations assume household alignment.

options.l: Yes — we've discussed and we're aligned

questions.label: Are you and your spouse aligned on retirement timing and what retirement looks like?
questions.help: The retirement-age decision is almost always made jointly by spouses (CL328 family-system framing); disagreement here delays or derails the entire decumulation arc.

options.l: Yes — same timeline and same picture of what retirement looks like
Mostly aligned, some differences in timing or vision

questions.label: Are you and your spouse aligned on whether to leave wealth to children / heirs vs spend it down per Die-with-Zero?
questions.help: Die-with-Zero trajectory only works without inheritance-expectation conflict among heirs (CL328) — and only with spousal agreement on the framing.

options.l: Yes — same view on legacy vs spend-down
